signals.title: BLADE: Auditing Information Use for Failure Attribution in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
signals.content: Large language model multi-agent systems extend individual agents' capabilities through collaboration across specialized roles, tools, and workflows. Yet collaboration makes failures harder to diagnose: one agent may misinterpret a correct result while others carry the mistake forward. Failure attribution therefore seeks to identify the responsible agent and decisive error step. Recent methods trace dependencies, but knowing where information came from is not the same as knowing where it went wrong. We introduce BLADE (Blame Localization via Audited Dependency Evidence), a training-free framework that moves beyond tracing information to auditing its use. Using Jev for structured probabilistic judgments, BLADE uses dependency probabilities to select relevant source-decision handoffs for auditing. At these handoffs, it examines whether receiving decisions use their sources faithfully and within task requirements, distinguishing error introduction, propagation, and repair. These findings inform a global diagnosis that considers all execution steps. Without reference answers, BLADE achieves the best or tied-best step accuracy among eight strategies under a shared Jev decision interface on 1,228 failed runs across five Who&When and Who&When Pro subsets, outperforming All-at-once by 2.2-11.1 percentage points. Making responsibility evidence explicit offers a path toward more interpretable and reliable agentic systems.

signals.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
signals.content: Agentic robotics places a large language model (LLM) agent in the robot control loop, where it composes perception, motion, and vision-language-action (VLA) tools under the guidance of a memory and thereby generalizes to new tasks without retraining. This generality comes at a steep price in efficiency. Every primitive requires a round of LLM reasoning over the full interaction history, so the cost of an episode grows with the number of primitives. We find this reasoning largely redundant: once a sub-goal is chosen, its primitives follow a routine already prescribed by memory. We present ChunkAct, which introduces action chunking to agentic robotics. Online, a single call launches a chunk of chained primitives, which executes autonomously and returns control only upon failure. Offline, ChunkAct compiles the memory into these chunks, so execution is memory-free at test time and the planner is reserved for decisions that require reasoning. LLM computation therefore scales with the number of decisions rather than the number of primitives. On LIBERO-Pro, ChunkAct improves task success by 5.0 points over the state of the art in agentic robotics while requiring 2.9x fewer LLM calls, 4.4x fewer input tokens, and 2.3x fewer output tokens.
signals.score_reason: academic/research signal; agentic AI relevance; large language model relevance; model capability relevance. Final score: 66. Freshness: source age 0.92d.
signals.brief_en: ChunkAct introduces action chunking to agentic robotics, allowing a single LLM call to launch a sequence of primitives that run autonomously until failure. By compiling memory‑based routines into reusable chunks, LLM reasoning is required only for high‑level decisions, reducing calls by 2.9×, input tokens by 4.4×, and output tokens by 2.3×. On the LIBERO‑Pro benchmark, ChunkAct raises task success by 5.0 points over the current state‑of‑the‑art, offering a more efficient path to general‑purpose robot control.
signals.brief_ar: يقدِّم ChunkAct تجزئة الإجراءات للروبوتات الوكيلة، حيث يُطلق استدعاء واحد للنموذج اللغوي سلسلة من الإجراءات التي تعمل autonomously حتى حدوث فشل. من خلال تجميع الروتينات المستندة إلى الذاكرة في قطع قابلة لإعادة الاستخدام، يُقتصر التفكير على القرارات العليا فقط، ما يقلل استدعاءات النموذج اللغوي بنسبة 2.9×، وتوكنات الإدخال بنسبة 4.4×، وتوكنات الإخراج بنسبة 2.3×. على معيار LIBERO‑Pro، يرفع ChunkAct نسبة نجاح المهمة بمقدار 5.0 نقطة مقارنةً بأحدث التقنيات، مما يوفر مسارًا أكثر كفاءة للتحكم العام في الروبوتات.

signals.title: MindFlock/MindFlock
signals.content: Run a flock of AI coding agents, each in its own git worktree, started by your ticket queue, merged by you. Work assigned to you in Jira, Linear, GitHub Issues, Shortcut or Asana becomes a seeded, already-running session; you review the diff and click it home.
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance; implementation ecosystem relevance. Final score: 65. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en: MindFlock is an AI‑driven orchestration layer that runs a flock of coding agents, each isolated in its own Git worktree. Tasks created in ticketing systems such as Jira, Linear, GitHub Issues, Shortcut or Asana automatically spawn a pre‑initialized agent session. The agent produces code changes, which are presented as a diff for human review and merge. The workflow enables rapid, parallel development while keeping final control with the reviewer.
signals.brief_ar: MindFlock هو طبقة تنظيمية مدعومة بالذكاء الاصطناعي تُشغِّل مجموعة من الوكلاء البرمجيين، كلٌّ في مساحة عمل Git منفصلة. تُنشئ أنظمة التذاكر مثل Jira أو Linear أو GitHub Issues أو Shortcut أو Asana مهامًا تُطلق جلسة وكيل مُهيَّأة مسبقًا. ينتج الوكيل تغييرات برمجية تُعرض كاختلاف للمراجعة البشرية قبل الدمج. يتيح هذا النموذج تطويرًا سريعًا ومتوازيًا مع الحفاظ على السيطرة النهائية للمراجِع.

signals.brief_en:
Title: engels-florentino/SocialCli
Brief: SocialCli is a command‑line interface designed for AI agents to interact with social media platforms. It enables agents to inspect public accounts, draft posts, and propose actions such as likes, follows, or comments. All actions are presented as previews for human approval before execution, and a local log records every interaction for auditability. The tool is intended for OSINT‑oriented, strategic use, emphasizing transparency and operator control while acknowledging the limits of automated social media manipulation.

signals.content: Skill and Agent Prompt Audit Tooling (scanner) | 技能与提示词安全审计（AI 技能审计器）
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance. Final score: 58. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: LGD-Eval/skill-audit

Tool: Skill and Agent Prompt Audit (scanner) – an OSINT‑style utility for systematic review of AI skill definitions and prompt safety. It parses skill manifests, extracts usage patterns, checks for ambiguous instructions, and flags potential privacy, bias, or security risks. Outputs a risk score and actionable remediation notes, supporting continuous compliance and strategic decision‑making.

Key capabilities:
- Automated syntax and schema validation of skill descriptors.
- Cross‑reference of prompts against known threat signatures and policy databases.
- Quantitative risk rating (0‑5) with confidence intervals.
- Export of audit logs for governance and audit trails.

Intended users: AI product managers, security analysts, compliance officers.

Limitations: Relies on up‑to‑date policy feeds; false positives possible; does not guarantee zero‑risk.

Strategic value: Enables proactive identification of unsafe or non‑compliant AI capabilities, reducing exposure and informing roadmap prioritization.

الأداة: فاحص المهارات وتعليمات الوكيل (المسح) – أداة OSINT منهجية لمراجعة تعريفات مهارات الذكاء الاصطناعي وسلامة التعليمات. تقوم بتحليل ملفات تعريف المهارات، استخراج أنماط الاستخدام، التحقق من الغموض في التعليمات، وتحديد مخاطر الخصوصية أو التحيز أو الأمن. تُنتج درجة خطر وملاحظات تصحيحية قابلة للتنفيذ، وتدعم الامتثال المستمر واتخاذ القرارات الاستراتيجية.

القدرات الرئيسية:
- التحقق الآلي من الصياغة والهيكلية لملفات المهارات.
- مقارنة التعليمات مع توقيعات التهديدات المعروفة وقواعد السياسات.
- تصنيف خطر كمي (0‑5) مع فواصل ثقة.
- تصدير سجلات الفحص لأغراض الحوكمة والتدقيق.

المستهدفون: مدراء منتجات الذكاء الاصطناعي، محللو الأمن، مسؤولو الامتثال.

القيود: يعتمد على تحديث مصادر السياسات؛ قد ينتج إيجابيات كاذبة؛ لا يضمن خلو المخاطر تمامًا.

القيمة الاستراتيجية: يتيح الكشف المبكر عن قدرات الذكاء الاصطناعي غير الآمنة أو غير المتوافقة، مما يقلل التعرض للمخاطر ويساعد في تحديد أولويات خارطة الطريق.

signals.brief_en:
Title: Filipe-Soares-de-Almeida/MemAI

Brief: MemAI is a long‑term memory MCP server designed for AI agents. It stores data in a single ACID‑compliant SQLite file with FTS5 BM25 full‑text search, supporting nested domain structures. The system includes diagram storage and a local curation dashboard for managing and visualising knowledge. Capabilities are documented, but operational performance and scalability in large‑scale deployments remain to be independently verified.

Title: pauljump/pricefixed
